meta.audience: All the people of Zarahemla, assembled at the temple
meta.location: The temple in the land of Zarahemla

world_behind.title: The king takes a poll
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has Benjamin sending among the people to find out whether they believed him. Nothing else in the record has a leader check. The covenant that follows is entered only after the answer comes back: consent before commitment.

world_behind.title: A name conferred, four chapters after it was promised
world_behind.text: Mosiah 1:12 announced a name that could only be lost through transgression. Here it arrives: the name of Christ. The whole address has been an approach to a single word.

world_behind.title: Adoption language, and its Israelite frame
world_behind.text: Sons and daughters, spiritually begotten, born of him. John says that to those who received him he gave power to become sons of God, to them that believe on his name. Benjamin reaches the same conclusion from a covenant ceremony.

world_behind.title: Right hand and left
world_behind.text: Verses 9 and 10 sort by which hand a person is found at. The sheep and the goats are divided the same way. What decides it here is whether the person knows the name he is called by.

world_behind.title: The stray animal, and the law behind it
world_behind.text: Verse 14 asks whether a man takes a neighbor's ass and keeps it. Exodus and Deuteronomy both oblige an Israelite to bring a wandering beast back to its owner, even an enemy's. Benjamin inverts the scene and shows an owner driving off a beast he cannot identify, and the whole figure turns on recognition.

words.text: Certainty, and in legal usage a guarantee backed by something. The people say they know of the truth's surety because of the Spirit. The Spirit is what backs the guarantee. Benjamin had told his sons they could know the records' surety because they had them before their eyes; his people now claim the same certainty from a different source.

Advantageous or fitting in the circumstances. The word carries more weight than convenient does. The people say they could prophesy of all things were it expedient. That is a restraint they place on themselves rather than a limit placed on them. It is the only qualification in an otherwise extraordinary claim.

A plural noun for what can be seen from where a person is standing. The people say they "have great views of that which is to come" (v. 3), and the word puts the future in front of them as something looked at. It is not in the King James Bible at all, and the record uses it only twice besides. What is being claimed is a sightline, and the rest of the verse turns that into a claim about prophesying.

cites.quote: have great views of that which is to come

spans.text: have great views of that which is to come

words.text: The verb does two jobs here and Benjamin uses both without marking the change. To be called the children of Christ, in verse 7, is to be named. To hear the voice by which ye shall be called, in verse 12, is to be summoned. This verse sits between them: whoever does not take the name upon him "must be called by some other name" (v. 10), and is then found on the left hand. The two senses run together, since a name is the thing a person answers to.

cites.quote: must be called by some other name

spans.text: must be called by some other name

words.text: Erased from a written record. The image belongs to ledgers and lists of names, and Benjamin has already used it once when the name was promised. The name is not taken away here; it is struck out, which assumes it was written down somewhere first.

Not merely unknown but outside the household. The King James sense is one who has no claim of belonging. Benjamin uses it of a master a man has never served, and the direction is the surprising part: the servant is the stranger to the master's thoughts.

phrases.term: Which has wrought a mighty change in us, or in our hearts
phrases.text: The people's own account of what happened to them, and the self-correction is the interesting part: in us, or more exactly in our hearts. The phrase enters the record here and Alma will build three consecutive questions on it, asking a congregation whether they have experienced this.

phrases.term: We have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually
phrases.text: A report about appetite. Disposition is what a person is inclined toward before choosing, and the claim is that the inclination itself has moved. It is the strongest description of conversion in the record and it is spoken by a crowd about itself.

phrases.term: We could prophesy of all things
phrases.text: An enormous claim, made in a subordinate clause, immediately qualified and then dropped. Nobody prophesies. The people mention the capacity and move straight on to the covenant, which seems to be what they are after.

phrases.term: We are willing to enter into a covenant with our God
phrases.text: The proposal comes from the people. Benjamin had asked only whether they believed; they answer that and then volunteer the obligation, name its terms (obedience in all things, all the remainder of their days), and state their reason. It is the angel's warning about the cup.

phrases.term: This day he hath spiritually begotten you
phrases.text: A birth dated to a specific day, and the evidence given is the changed heart the people reported two verses earlier. Benjamin reasons backward from their own testimony: you say your hearts are changed, therefore you are born of him. The logic runs from experience to status.

phrases.term: Under this head ye are made free, and there is no other head
phrases.text: "Head" in the sense of the one you stand under. The clause pairs freedom with subjection in the same breath and says there is no alternative arrangement. The point is not that other heads are worse, but that freedom is available under one only.

phrases.term: I would that ye should take upon you the name of Christ
phrases.text: The instruction the whole address has been building toward, and it is phrased as something the hearer does. Benjamin has just said they are already begotten and already called; the taking is theirs to do anyway.

phrases.term: He shall know the name by which he is called
phrases.text: Knowing the name is the qualification, not bearing it. Verse 12 says the same thing about hearing and knowing the voice. What the chapter requires is recognition on both sides, and the final verses are all about what happens when recognition fails.

phrases.term: Retain the name written always in your hearts
phrases.text: The name is to be kept in writing, in a person, permanently. It answers the blotting-out of the previous verse: the register the name can be struck from is the heart. The record's whole preoccupation with engraving is put inside a human being.

phrases.term: How knoweth a man the master whom he has not served
phrases.text: Service as the means of knowledge. The question assumes that acquaintance with a master comes from working for him and cannot be had another way, which turns the chapter's talk of names into a claim about time spent. The unserved master is a stranger to the man's thoughts and intents.

phrases.term: Doth a man take an ass which belongeth to his neighbor, and keep him?
phrases.text: A property question, and the answer is that the owner drives off a beast he does not recognize. Israelite law required returning a stray to its owner; the figure here is what happens to an animal with no recognizable owner at all. Benjamin says: even so shall it be among you.

phrases.term: Steadfast and immovable, always abounding in good works
phrases.text: Paul's charge to the Corinthians, with "work of the Lord" changed to "good works." Two adjectives about not moving, followed by a participle about not stopping. The combination is the chapter's picture of a covenant kept: fixed in position, busy in practice.

phrases.term: That Christ, the Lord God Omnipotent, may seal you his
phrases.text: The last act belongs to Christ. After a chapter in which the people volunteer, propose, and take a name upon themselves, the sealing is done to them. The title used is the one the angel introduced two chapters earlier.

verses.label: v. 1–4
verses.title: The answer
verses.text: Benjamin sends to ask whether they believed; they cry with one voice that they do and that they know its surety because of the Spirit; a mighty change has been wrought in their hearts and they have no more disposition to evil; they have great views of what is coming and could prophesy if it were expedient; and faith in what their king said brought them here. Four verses of the congregation describing itself.

verses.label: v. 5–6
verses.title: The covenant, offered and accepted
verses.text: They are willing to enter into it, to obey in all things for the rest of their lives, so as not to bring never-ending torment on themselves or drink the cup the angel spoke of. Benjamin replies that these are the words he wanted and the covenant is righteous. Nobody asked them.

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: The name
verses.text: Because of the covenant they are called the children of Christ, sons and daughters, spiritually begotten this day, born of him, because they said their hearts were changed. Under this head they are free and there is no other; no other name saves; therefore take the name upon you and be obedient to the end.

verses.label: v. 9–10
verses.title: Two hands
verses.text: Whoever does this is found at the right hand and knows the name he is called by; whoever does not must be called by some other name and finds himself at the left. The sorting criterion is stated twice and both times it is knowledge of a name rather than a tally of deeds.

verses.label: v. 11–12
verses.title: Keep it written
verses.text: This is the name promised earlier, which only transgression can erase; so take heed, and retain it written always in your hearts, so that you are not found at the left hand but hear and know the voice that will call you, and the name he will use.

verses.label: v. 13–14
verses.title: Two questions about not knowing
verses.text: How does a man know a master he has not served, who is a stranger to his thoughts? And does a man keep a neighbor's stray animal? No; he drives it off. Two figures, both about recognition, and the second is harsher than the first.

verses.label: v. 15
verses.title: The charge
verses.text: Steadfast, immovable, abounding in good works, so that Christ may seal you his and bring you to heaven, with everlasting salvation and eternal life, through his wisdom, power, justice, and mercy. One verse, and it is the last thing Benjamin says in the address.

chapter.title: The covenant is volunteered
chapter.text: Benjamin asked one question, whether they believed, and the people answered it and then offered an obligation he had not requested, in words he then confirms were the ones he wanted. Nothing is imposed anywhere in the chapter, and the chapter is the climax of the address.

chapter.title: Conversion is reported as a change in appetite
chapter.text: "No more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually" is not a promise about future conduct; it is a claim about what they now want. The record's fullest description of a changed heart is spoken by the people themselves, about themselves, in the plural.

chapter.title: The name is the whole point of six chapters
chapter.text: Promised in Mosiah 1:12, withheld through the address, and given here. Every part of the assembly is arranged around one word being conferred: the gathering, the tents, the angel's message, the falling down, the covenant.

chapter.title: Belonging is described as mutual recognition
chapter.text: He shall know the name by which he is called; ye shall hear and know the voice; how knoweth a man the master he has not served. The chapter's danger is anonymity: being unrecognized, and not recognizing.

chapter.title: The two figures at the end are about ownership
chapter.text: A servant who never served, and an animal nobody claims. Neither is accused of anything. What disqualifies them is that no relationship exists, which is a different kind of warning than the one Mosiah 3 gave.

chapter.title: Freedom and subjection are stated together
chapter.text: "Under this head ye are made free." The sentence does not soften either half or explain the paradox, and it forecloses alternatives in the same breath. No other head, no other name.

chapter.title: The last act is not the covenanter's
chapter.text: The people volunteer, propose, take the name, and are told to be steadfast; and then Christ seals them his. After a chapter of initiative from below, the closing verb belongs to someone else.

applications.title: Ask before you assume
applications.text: Benjamin checked whether he had been understood before proceeding. After teaching or explaining anything that matters, ask plainly whether it landed.

applications.title: Volunteer the obligation
applications.text: The people offered a commitment nobody required of them. Identify one thing you have been waiting to be asked to do, and offer it instead.

applications.title: Test for disposition
applications.text: Ask what you now want. The chapter's marker of real change is appetite, and appetite is harder to fake than resolution.

applications.title: Serve in order to know
applications.text: If God feels like a stranger, the chapter's diagnosis is unserved rather than unknowable. Pick something to do for him this week and notice what it teaches you.

applications.title: Keep the name written
applications.text: Retaining is a daily act. Decide what in your ordinary week actually keeps the name in front of you, and protect that thing.

applications.title: Be fixed and busy at once
applications.text: Steadfast, immovable, always abounding. Name one commitment you will not move on, and one form of good work you will keep doing regardless of how you feel.

questions.text: Has my disposition changed, or only my behavior, and would I know the difference?
What have I been willing to do only if asked?
What else am I standing under, and does it make me free?
If I were called by name today, would I recognize the voice?
How much time have I actually spent serving the one I say I know?
Is there anything about me that would identify whose I am, to someone watching?
Am I steadfast without being busy, or busy without being steadfast?
